title: patchwork-lit-notes-raman-2028-06
content:
Patchwork lit + quick experiments (scratchpad)

Goal: collect diverse ideas about stitching/compressing/sharding KV cache for latency-sensitive multi-tenant inference. Make a shortlist of hypotheses we can microbench on a dedicated 4xA100 rig.

High-level takeaways (3 papers skimmed today):
1) PatchworkKV (arXiv:2806.12345) — idea: break long context into overlapping micro-shards, compress each shard with inexpensive lossy transform, reconstruct on-demand.
  - Pros: lower memory per host, cheaper multi-tenant consolidation.
  - Cons: reconstruction cost + staleness if shard boundaries misalign with attention windows.
  - Note: Paper uses simple PCA per-shard; seems cheap but might lose high-frequency token signals (names, dates).

2) Eviction-by-surprise (conf-proc 2027) — compute eviction score = alpha*recency + beta*surprise; surprise approximated with next-token entropy delta when chunk is used.
  - Implementation thought: keep moving-average entropy per chunk (ema with tau=200 requests). Score update cheap (1 add, 1 multiply).
  - Risk: need small counters per chunk -> memory overhead. Could quantize counters to 8 bits.

3) Shard-routing for hetero-GPUs (sysnet'26) — route requests to GPUs with partial cache hits and on-the-fly stitching. Uses RDMA and sub-token pipelining to hide stitch latency.
  - Interesting: runtime uses earlier tokens to predict whether a shard will be needed; prefetch pipeline if probability > 0.6.

Open hypotheses for Redwood:
- H1: Micro-shard compression + partial reconstruction yields >1.5x reduction in resident KV memory with <7% P99 latency increase for Chat-like workloads (seq=2k, few-shot).
- H2: Eviction-by-surprise reduces token-level recompute by ~20% vs LRU under conversational workloads.
- H3: Prefetch-on-probability with cheap predictor (sigmoid over last-token embedding dot) can hide reconstruction latency at P99 for many requests.

Mini-experiment plan (fast, 1d sprint):
- Bench harness: reuse local/bench client (bench-client:v0.3) against policy-sim traces (customer-A conv trace, 48k requests).
- Implement toy micro-shard: fixed 256-token shards, compress with 8-bit PCA (numpy) -> store quantized vectors. On reconstruction, dequantize + add residual table for top-16 dimensions.
- Metric set: resident-KV-memory, avg-token-latency, p95/p99 end-to-end, extra-reconstruct-CPU-cycles.
- Baseline: current kv-cache (no compression, chunk size=1024).

Implementation notes/sketches:
- Shard keying: session-id + floor(token_index / 256). Meta: last_access_ts, access_count (8-bit), ema_entropy (16-bit fixed point).
- Eviction score = w1*(now-last_access) + w2*(ema_entropy). Normalize weights by percentiles from live trace.
- Prefetch predictor: dot(last_token_embedding, shard_summary_vector) -> sigmoid -> threshold 0.6. Shard_summary_vector = avg of first-8 token embeddings of shard (precomputed).

Edge cases / open questions (notes to self):
- How to handle overlapping shards for rolling windows? overlapping=sliding by 128 tokens reduce boundary loss but double metadata entries. Tradeoff analysis needed.
- What is cost profile of PCA compression vs simple uniform scalar quantization? Implementation simplicity favors scalar Q but may lose correlation structure which matters for attention.
- Security: compressed shards still in memory; do we need different KMS semantics? Probably not but note for Private deployments (customer legal ask).

Slack TODOs / followups:
- @Maya: can you pull 1 week of conv-trace for customer-A (ideally >40k reqs) and drop in /bench/traces? (slack thread: #kv-cache-ops)
- @Omar: quick check if bench-client supports on-demand dequantize hook; if not add simple callback. PR placeholder: github.com/redwood-inference/kv-patchwork/pull/87
- Create JIRA ticket for microbench job (JIRA-ENG-4321).

Quick sketches of expected numbers (back-of-envelope):
- Resident KV tokens per session baseline: 25k tokens -> ~25k*768*4 bytes ~ 76.8 MB per session (float32).
- With 8-bit quant + PCA(64)-> store 64 dims as int8 + 64 bytes for PCA basis ~ 16 KB/session? Need to re-evaluate exact math. This looks optimistic; recompute once we have real vectors.

Short meeting agenda (15m sync) with Maya/Omar:
- 0-3m: quick readouts from traces (size, seq distrib)
- 3-7m: outline toy micro-shard impl + responsibilities
- 7-12m: pick metrics, decide baseline sampling window
- 12-15m: next steps + ownership (Maya: traces, Omar: bench infra, Raman: proto impl)

Random notes / brain-dump:
- Might reuse quantization primitives from redwood/optimize (check repo: github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/quant).
- Consider hybrid approach: keep hot shards uncompressed, tier cold shards to compressed store (spill to NVMe). That matches Dedicated offering where local SSD available.
- Long-term: tie quality regression to prompt-set evals (Redwood Optimize flow): if compression introduces >1.5% ROUGE/accuracy regression on devset then reject patch.

References to collect (links to add):
- arXiv:2806.12345 (PatchworkKV)
- ConfPaperID: Eviction-by-Surprise 2027
- SysNet'26: Shard-routing for hetero-GPUs
- internal GH: github.com/redwood-inference/kv-patchwork
- internal Confluence: /display/INFR/PatchworkKV-proposal

End-of-scratchpad. Save this, then convert top bits into PR description once toy benchmarks confirm H1/H2.

Notes-to-self: keep notes messy here; will produce a cleaned draft for PR and Confluence if experiments look promising.
